JIEJIE.NET_2026-01-01_dotnet8_cil_consol.build_flags: dotnet build JIEJIENETForCore.Console.csproj -c Debug (upstream's configuration: DefineConstants TRACE;DOTNETCORE, AllowUnsafeBlocks, Optimize=false), netcoreapp3.1, -p:ContinuousIntegrationBuild=true -p:PathMap=<checkout>=/_/
JIEJIE.NET_2026-01-01_dotnet8_cil_consol.notes: The obfuscator's own code, not its output. FortiGuard Labs (2026-08-04) says the generation-2 FDMTP loader Microsoft.ServiceHosting.Tools.dll in the QuickFox supply-chain attack 'is obfuscated using the JieJie .NET Protector tool'; that sentence is the only evidence, no code comparison is shown, and nothing here was checked against that sample. A protected assembly does not contain this engine, so this family recognises JIEJIE.NET itself. 59 of the 858 methods are namespace __DC20211119 (JIEJIEHelper, JIEJIEPerformanceCounter), the C# source of the helpers the tool injects into protected assemblies as IL text; whether they match the injected copies was not measured. Upstream's committed binaries are Debug builds, so both configurations are built. Pinned to f28e1d2, the last commit touching source/; the version the attackers used is unknown. The .NET Framework console is not built: its project file is committed E-SafeNet-encrypted. Components gui_debug and gui_release: the .NET Framework 4.0 WinForms GUI of the same engine and commit (JIEJIE.NET.GUI.csproj), built with the .NET SDK's MSBuild. The SDK MSBuild refuses the form's embedded System.Drawing bitmaps (MSB3822/MSB3823) unless resources are generated preserialized, which needs a System.Resources.Extensions reference: the recipe adds one (package 5.0.0, pinned) through a targets file passed with CustomAfterMicrosoftCommonTargets, and takes the v4.0 reference assemblies from Microsoft.NETFramework.ReferenceAssemblies.net40 1.0.3. No upstream file is modified, but the build adds a reference the project does not declare and writes the .resources in the preserialized format, so the gui images are NOT byte-identical to a build of unmodified upstream with full-Framework MSBuild. Upstream's committed binaries are Debug builds, so both configurations are built. 905 methods in each; of the Debug image's 691 distinct PicHashes of ten instructions or more, 633 are in the Core console Debug artefact (Release: 562 of 616 in the console Release).
